doc.title: John LaPorta interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 13, 1996

chapter: Race, feel and playing with Mingus
title: Playing with black and white groups
summary: His early influences were Lester Young and Duke, so white Dixieland sessions called his notes wrong while black sessions felt like home.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: evident qualities. Of course I had problems playing with white groups because my influences were black when I was young. When I first started hearing records around the age of sixteen, seventeen, I got into Lester Young and Duke and you know their music. Whenever I went to a white session and sat in, of course they were playing Dixieland music, and they’d accuse me of playing wrong notes and everything else, it was what I heard. And then I’d play in a black session and nobody seemed to be bugged about the so-called wrong notes I was playing see, so I felt like I was at home. So I’ve always had that kind of sort of contradiction going on in my life.
